verses.text: King Darius issued an order, and they searched the archives in Babylon where the treasures were kept.
They found a scroll at Achmetha, in the palace in the province of Media. Here’s what it recorded:

In his first year as king, Cyrus issued this order about God’s house in Jerusalem: Rebuild the house, the place where sacrifices are offered, and lay a solid foundation. It is to be sixty cubits high and sixty cubits wide,
with three layers of large stones and a layer of new timber. The royal household is to pay the expenses.

Return the gold and silver vessels from God’s house that Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in Jerusalem to Babylon. Bring them back to the temple in Jerusalem and put each one in its place in God’s house.
So now, Tattenai, governor beyond the River, Shetharbozenai, and your Apharsachite companions beyond the River, stay well away from there.
Leave the work on this house of God alone. Let the Jewish governor and elders rebuild God’s house on its own site.
I’m also ordering you to help these Jewish elders rebuild God’s house. Pay their expenses promptly from the royal funds collected as tribute beyond the River so nothing holds them up.

Give them whatever they need every single day, as the priests in Jerusalem direct: young bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, as well as wheat, salt, wine, and oil. Don’t miss a day.
Then they can offer sacrifices with a pleasing aroma to the God of heaven and pray for the lives of the king and his sons.

I also order that if anyone changes this decree, a beam is to be pulled out of their house. They’re to be lifted up and fastened to it, and their house is to be turned into a dung heap because of what they did.
May the God who made his name dwell there overthrow any king or people who try to change this decree or destroy his house in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued this order. Get it done without delay.
Tattenai, the governor beyond the River, Shetharbozenai, and their companions carried it out promptly because King Darius had sent the order.

The Jewish elders kept building, and the work went well through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo. They finished the building as the God of Israel had commanded and as Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia had decreed.
They finished the house on the third day of Adar in the sixth year of King Darius’s reign.
The Israelites, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of those who’d returned from exile celebrated the dedication of God’s house with joy.
To dedicate God’s house, they offered one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs. For a sin offering for all Israel, they brought twelve male goats, one for each tribe of Israel.
They assigned the priests and Levites to their groups for serving God in Jerusalem, just as it’s written in the book of Moses.
Those who’d come back from exile celebrated Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.

The priests and Levites had purified themselves together, so they were all clean. They slaughtered the Passover animals for everyone who’d returned from exile, for their fellow priests, and for themselves.
The Israelites who’d returned from exile ate the meal. So did everyone who’d joined them after turning away from the unclean practices of the peoples of the land to seek the LORD, the God of Israel.

They joyfully celebrated the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days. The LORD had given them that joy by turning the heart of the king of Assyria toward them so he would give them a hand with the work on the house of God, the God of Israel.
